title: bus message
description: One message on the bus: a file inboxes/<agent>/[@<slug>/]<id>.json, written atomically (tmp + rename). 'version' stays "1.0": every field added since (from_session, context.host) is optional and additive, and readers MUST ignore fields they do not know. Two machines (v2.5): the same file travels unchanged; the session and the machine of the RECIPIENT live in the path (inboxes/, or outbox/<host>/ while in transit with the same layout), not in 'to'. Written by the bash lib and agent-bus-mcp in the canonical shape; hand-written messages exist on real buses (no version, custom ids, other priorities), so the schema only requires what routing needs and readers MUST be lenient.

id.description: Also the file name. Canonical form msg-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>-<rand8>, which sorts by time.

version.description: "1.0" from the lib and the MCP server.

from_session.description: Optional. Sender agent and session, 'agent/slug' (written by agent-bus-mcp). Lets a reply reach that session.

to.description: Recipient agent, ALWAYS the bare name (no /slug, no @host): readers and threads stay unchanged.

thread_id.description: Travels with the message, so a thread continues across machines.

type.description: request | brief | question | response | accept | decline | confirm | event | handoff | cc-notify

priority.description: Canonical: low | normal | high | urgent. Anything else reads as normal.

payload.description: Free form; 'summary' is shown in listings.

context_refs.description: Usually absolute paths; older messages carry objects ({type, path}).

context.description: Optional. Where the message comes from and what it is about.

host.description: v2.5. Machine of the SENDER (its $AB_HOME/HOST, or the hub host). Absent on a single-machine bus. A reply goes to from@host (see ab_reply_address / Bus.reply_address).

project_path.description: v1.2 workspace filter: the message is about this folder.
